name: Global Payments

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Global Payments Inc. logo.svg)

description: Global Payments is a merchant-acquiring and payments-technology company: it processes card payments for businesses and takes a percentage of each transaction or a fee per transaction, and sells point-of-sale and business software to small businesses. In January 2026 it swapped businesses with FIS: it bought Worldpay (large-enterprise and e-commerce acquiring) and sold its Issuer Solutions card-processing business (the old TSYS) to FIS, so after January 2026 it is nearly a pure merchant-acquiring company. It now reports three segments (Enterprise, Platforms, SMB) after the Worldpay integration. The 2026 first half is therefore not comparable with 2025.

employees.note: Approximately 26,000 team members in 37 countries at 2025-12-31, before the Worldpay acquisition closed in January 2026 and the Issuer Solutions divestiture.

businessLines.name: Enterprise
businessLines.how: Large and multinational merchants pay a percentage of transaction value or a fee per transaction for card-present and card-not-present (online) acceptance, plus value-added software; Worldpay brought most of this segment.

businessLines.name: Platforms
businessLines.how: Software partners, payment facilitators and marketplaces embed Global Payments acceptance; it earns a share of the processing fees on volume those platforms generate (revenue-share model, volume-driven).

businessLines.name: SMB (Small and Medium-Sized Businesses)
businessLines.how: Small merchants pay per-transaction and percentage fees for card acceptance, monthly fees for point-of-sale technology and business-management software, sold directly and through partners.

businessLines.name: Other (not in the three segments)
businessLines.how: Revenue outside the three reportable segments; not described separately in the 10-Q.

brands.name: Worldpay
brands.note: Acquired January 2026 (from FIS and GTCR): $6.2B cash plus 43.3 million Global Payments shares to GTCR; Worldpay provisional goodwill $10.0B of which $8.8B Enterprise

brands.name: Heartland
brands.note: US small-business processing and software brand (payroll business sold to Acrisure for about $1.1B, September 2025)

brands.name: Issuer Solutions (TSYS)
brands.note: Divested to FIS January 2026 for about $7.7B cash plus FIS's ownership interest in Worldpay; presented as discontinued operations

brands.name: Heartland Payroll Solutions
brands.note: Sold to Acrisure September 2025 for about $1.1B including up to $75M contingent

brands.name: AdvancedMD
brands.note: Sold December 2024 for about $1.1B plus up to $125M contingent
